description: Registered suppressions. Every live suppression directive (oxlint, eslint, ts-expect-error, ts-ignore, ts-nocheck) must match an entry by file and directive, and every entry needs a live suppression. An entry names its scope, reason, native alternatives examined, owner, versions and retirement trigger.

exceptions.reason: kokoro-js (from_pretrained, generate) and the dynamic imports that keep onnxruntime-node unloaded on a cache hit return Promises. Each is wrapped once as Effect.tryPromise with a non-async thunk, as EX-0030 and EX-0040 do; typescript/promise-function-async wants those thunks async and its autofix then trips eslint/require-await and effecttsgo/async-function, so the rule is disabled on the four thunk lines only. The file is the speech-kokoro package's only Promise boundary.
nativeAlternativesExamined: Effect.tryPromise with an async thunk: effecttsgo/async-function (Effect diagnostic, error) rejects it and eslint/require-await rejects an async function that only returns the Promise
Effect.promise and Effect.callback: the same Promise-returning thunk, so the same conflict
One helper `promised(run)` with a single directive: the arrow at each call site is itself a function that returns a Promise, so the rule still fires there
Stream.fromAsyncIterable over KokoroTTS.stream: streams sentence chunks, no cancellation, and would still need the dynamic imports and from_pretrained Promises
a child process running kokoro: no CLI ships with kokoro-js, and the 311 MiB model would load once per Line
exceptions.retirementTrigger: typescript/promise-function-async stops flagging thunks passed to Effect.tryPromise, or kokoro-js is replaced by an Effect-native text-to-speech client

exceptions.reason: The deck tests' browser adapter drives Playwright, whose API returns Promises. Every call is wrapped once, as Effect.promise or Effect.tryPromise with a thunk; typescript/promise-function-async wants those thunks to be async, and its autofix then adds await and trips eslint/require-await and effecttsgo/async-function.
nativeAlternativesExamined: Effect.promise and Effect.tryPromise take a thunk that returns the Promise; they have no overload that takes a method and its arguments.
Making the thunks async: effecttsgo/async-function is an Effect diagnostic at error severity and eslint/require-await rejects an async function that only returns the Promise.
An Effect-native browser driver: none in the installed effect 4.0.6 or @effect/platform-node 4.0.6.
exceptions.retirementTrigger: An Effect-native browser driver ships in the installed Effect packages, or the lint preset stops flagging thunks passed straight to Effect.promise and Effect.tryPromise.

exceptions.reason: The Browser service adapts Playwright, whose API returns Promises. Each call is wrapped once, in `inPage`, as `Effect.tryPromise({ try: () => page.method(...) })`; typescript/promise-function-async wants those arrow functions to be `async`, and its autofix then adds `await` and trips eslint/require-await and effecttsgo/async-function.

An Effect-native browser driver: none in the installed effect 4.0.6 or @effect/platform-node 4.0.6.
